tagline: One of the nation's largest owners and operators of grocery-anchored shopping centers
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is the primary driver of operating performance in the REIT real estate sector, reflecting organic growth in rental revenues and portfolio quality. It captures leasing trends, occupancy, and cost management across a comparable property base.

kpis.name: Same-Center NOI
kpis.explanation: Net revenues from properties held throughout the period, excluding acquisitions and dispositions.
kpis.description: Same-Center NOI measures operating performance of continuously held properties. It excludes the effects of acquisitions, dispositions, and corporate overhead.

kpis.name: Occupancy Rate
kpis.explanation: Percentage of leasable space occupied in the real estate portfolio.
kpis.description: An occupancy rate of 97.3% indicates a well-occupied portfolio with minimal vacancy.
kpis.signal: Very high occupancy rate, reflecting strong leasing demand

kpis.name: Core FFO per Share
kpis.explanation: Key profitability measure for REITs, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Core FFO excludes non-recurring items such as acquisition costs or disposition gains, providing a clearer view of recurring performance.
kpis.signal: Core FFO per share growth supported by leasing performance

kpis.name: EBITDA re
kpis.explanation: EBITDA adjusted to reflect operating performance of real estate assets.
kpis.description: EBITDA re is a non-GAAP measure that excludes depreciation and gains/losses on dispositions, useful for comparing REIT performance.
kpis.signal: EBITDA re growth of +10.1%, driven by higher rental rates

kpis.name: Total Portfolio Size
kpis.explanation: Total leasable square footage in the portfolio, including non-consolidated interests.
kpis.description: Total portfolio comprises properties owned outright and via joint ventures, distributed across demographically strong markets.
kpis.signal: Portfolio of 36.7 million square feet across 31 states

kpis.name: Number of Wholly-Owned Properties
kpis.explanation: Number of shopping centers owned 100% by the company.
kpis.description: These assets generate the majority of the company's rental revenues.
kpis.signal: 297 wholly-owned properties, providing a solid base of recurring revenues

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of $5.29B in the most recent year

kpis.name: Total Debt
kpis.description: Total debt extracted from yfinance over the last 4 years.
kpis.signal: Total debt of $2.49B in the most recent year

kpis.name: Same-Center NOI
kpis.explanation: Net revenues from properties held throughout the period, excluding acquisitions and dispositions.
kpis.description: Growth of +3.8% in 2025, driven by rental rate increases and strong occupancy.

kpis.name: Core FFO per Share
kpis.explanation: Key profitability measure for REITs, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Core FFO grows due to higher NOI and efficient cost management.

risks.title: Cyberattacks impacting business continuity
risks.score_rationale: The risk is explicitly mentioned first in the risk factors under 'Risks Related to Business Continuity and Cybersecurity'. The language indicates a significant operational risk that could disrupt critical systems. Cybersecurity is highly weighted in the context of digitally managed real estate. Central positioning in the 10-K reinforces its importance.

risks.title: Dependence on economic conditions
risks.score_rationale: The document directly links rental growth to economic health and occupancy rates. Repeated mention of recession sensitivity. Strong forward-looking language ('may experience rental rate decline'). Central macroeconomic risk to rental revenues. Highly weighted category.

risks.title: Lease renewal risk in 2026
risks.score_rationale: 735 leases expiring in 2026 covering 2.7 million square feet. While occupancy is high at 97.3%, lease renewal at lower rates is an explicit risk. Detailed discussion in 'Lease Expirations'. Cautious language regarding ability to predict new rates.

risks.title: Geographic concentration in Florida
risks.score_rationale: 12.3% of ABR derives from Florida, the leading state. Concentration risk not explicitly mentioned but implied given exposure to natural disasters or local regulation. High position in geographic table. Moderately weighted category.

risks.title: Dependence on few large tenants
risks.score_rationale: Top 3 tenants (Kroger, Publix, Albertsons) represent 13.7% of ABR. While diversified, failure of a major tenant would have notable impact. Mentioned in 'Top 20 Neighbors'. Moderate but material risk.

risks.title: Ordinary legal risk not currently materialized
risks.score_rationale: Document mentions routine legal proceedings but specifies none are reasonably likely to have material impact. Reassuring language ('not reasonably likely'). End-of-section positioning. Moderately weighted category but current risk is low.

ai_positioning.summary: PECO does not mention artificial intelligence or machine learning in its 10-K/20-F filing.
